description: This line plot illustrates the average performance, measured as a percentage, of three metrics—Precision, Recall, and F1-score—across different model sizes, ranging from 70 million parameters to 7 billion parameters. The x-axis represents model size, labeled in units of "m" (million) and "B" (billion), with tick marks at 70m, 160m, 410m, 1.0B, 1.4B, 2.8B, and 7.0B, and uses a linear scale. The y-axis represents "Avg. Performance (%)" and ranges from 0 to 80, also on a linear scale. The red line with triangle markers represents Precision, which starts at approximately 78% at 70m, slightly declines to about 70% at 410m, and then remains relatively stable near 75% up to 7.0B. The blue line with triangle markers represents Recall, which begins at approximately 10% at 70m, increases to about 20% at 410m, and continues rising to approximately 45% at 7.0B. The purple line with triangle markers represents F1-score, which starts at approximately 16% at 70m, rises to about 30% at 410m, and increases further to approximately 58% at 7.0B. All three lines show an upward trend as model size increases, with F1-score consistently increasing the most and Precision remaining the highest throughout.
